status: Fixed in source; frozen publication pending
area: One command needing two emergency permissions cannot be authorized at all
finding: tasks close with --allow-stale-runner and --historical-delivery selects two protected surfaces: the stale-runner path requires backend.runnerRecovery and the close itself requires backend.tasks.close. --emergency-approval binds exactly one lease, and each check reports only the permission it wanted, so every single-lease attempt is refused by whichever check the lease does not satisfy. Passing both leases does not help: the last one parsed wins and the other check fails. The emergency lane is therefore closed to any operation that legitimately needs two permissions, which is precisely the operation most likely to need it.
expectedBehavior: --emergency-approval must accept a set of leases and satisfy each protected surface from whichever lease authorizes it, or an approve call must be able to grant a bounded permission set in one lease. Each permission must stay individually bounded to task, actor and flags, and the refusal must name every permission still unsatisfied rather than only the first one checked — an operator who is told one permission at a time cannot tell a two-permission command from a wrong lease.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0367, 2026-08-13. Four leases were approved in sequence. EMG-ATM-GOV-0367-3ea985dbab (backend.tasks.close, --allow-stale-runner) refused with ATM_EMERGENCY_FLAG_NOT_APPROVED for --historical-delivery. EMG-ATM-GOV-0367-e3b96a26e7 (backend.tasks.close, both flags) refused with ATM_EMERGENCY_PERMISSION_MISMATCH: is for backend.tasks.close, not backend.runnerRecovery. EMG-ATM-GOV-0367-ba958cfa28 (backend.runnerRecovery, both flags) refused with the mirror image: is for backend.runnerRecovery, not backend.tasks.close. Passing ba958cfa28 and e3b96a26e7 together refused on whichever was named second. The card was delivered as 0cf861814 and could not be closed through this lane at all; the blocker was cleared by removing the stale-runner condition itself. Publication verified on 2026-08-14 against the runner's own declared input: release/atm-onefile/release-manifest.json at publication commit 8a3047111c7eb3673950ae719daed2801c151860 records sealedSourceCommit b3996c755027679acd995c4163fe96365f20468b with buildDecision fullRebuild and payloadReuse false, so the packed runner was rebuilt from that commit rather than reusing an earlier payload. The fix commit for this item, 50e806e85d8166cda1961d170bc4f6f16de3c8bd, is an ancestor of that sealed source commit. Corroborated inside the published tree by direct symbol: packages/cli/dist/commands/emergency/gate.js at 8a3047111c7eb3673950ae719daed2801c151860 contains selectLeaseForPermission and the suppliedLeases refusal payload. Independently confirmed in use: ATM-GOV-0368 was itself closed through the frozen runner by passing two lease ids as one comma-separated --emergency-approval value, which is the exact capability this item was refused.
followUp: Fixed in source by ATM-GOV-0368. The approval argument gained set semantics without changing its type: a single --emergency-approval value may carry comma-separated lease ids, and assertEmergencyApproval selects the member whose permission matches the surface being authorized, consuming only that member. Selection is the entire change — each selected lease is still validated for status, permission, task, actor, expiry, remaining uses and allowed flags exactly as a lone lease always was, so nothing an operator must approve became optional, and every call site that forwards the value as a string was left untouched. When no member matches, the refusal now lists every supplied lease with the permission it carries alongside the permission required, which is the same disclosure correction made for lane refusals in [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-021]. Regression guard: test_atm_gov_0368_one_command_satisfies_every_permission_it_needs in packages/cli/src/commands/emergency/__tests__/gate.test.ts, which asserts the two-surface case selects a different lease per surface, that each is consumed exactly once, and that a set covering neither surface is still refused with no lease consumed. Before that fix existed, the only route was to remove the second condition rather than authorize it — republish the frozen runner so --allow-stale-runner is not needed — which is available only to an operator who can also take the release surface, and which was tried here and did not hold. ATM-GOV-0367 took the release surface, reserved the runner-sync queue head, rebuilt the sealed runner from f1fa1208c and committed the artifacts as 652d48a5c; the runner was current for roughly three minutes. A second lane then created an untracked file under scripts/, whose mtime post-dated the build, and the freshness check declared the runner stale again — the same live-WIP sensitivity recorded in [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-019], here reached through the staleness check rather than through publication admission. The consequence is worth stating plainly: while any other lane is actively editing framework source, no amount of republishing makes a close reachable, and the emergency lane that exists for exactly that case is the dead end above. Either half alone is survivable; together they close every route. The mechanism is worth stating exactly, because it makes the deadlock permanent rather than transient: freshness is judged by mtime, while the sealed build is content-cached. Re-running the build at the new HEAD returned cacheHitSkip — correctly, since no framework source had changed — so no artifact mtime advanced and the runner stayed stale. Once any foreign file's mtime passes the last build, a lane that has changed no source cannot make the runner fresh again by rebuilding, because the only honest build is a no-op. The deadlock lifts only when someone else's genuine source change triggers a real rebuild. Related to [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-013], the bootstrap circularity that makes --allow-stale-runner necessary in the first place, and to [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-021] in that both are refusals that disclose one side of a two-sided comparison.
